subject: p-fc
title: (R)P.FC.------POL.P.
description: Diagram in AE(PD)-5 (Aspect Essence / Perception Dynamics, Level One) opening Braxton's central frame for the chapter: the sixties activism analysis. 'The vibrational platform that solidified in the sixties would establish the first real move towards alternative functionalism for the post–World War Two generation.' (R)P-FC (the reality of point-focus) is crossed with POL-P (political particulars): the question is what point-focus produces in its actual instantiation when crossed with political-particulars — the (R) prefix marking that this is about the *real* focal-point at which sixties activism intervened, not a conceptual one. EXT-INFO (extended information) sits between subject and partner. MT-INFO (multi-information) feeds in from the upper-left. POL-P sits at the upper-right. TRS (transference) hangs below EXT-INFO. POST (postulation) anchors the lower-center. OP-SPD (option-spread) hangs on the lower-right. SOC-RT-DY (social-reality dynamics) sits between point-focus and the lower output. CULT-SOLD (culture solidification) anchors the lower-center. Structural argument: point-focus-as-real crossed with political-particulars is mediated by extended-information as central hub, with multi-information as upstream and option-spread as marginal output. The diagram exposes Braxton's structural diagnostic of sixties activism: real point-focus crossed with political-particulars produces option-spread (multiple alternative paths) and feeds into culture-solidification through postulation and social-reality-dynamics. The schematic is the case for why the early sixties activism was productive — point-focus was *real* (not styled), and the productive output ran through three lower upstream tests (transference, postulation, social-reality-dynamics) into culture-solidification.
